==English== {{wp}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alter|en|joyn|joyne|joyen||obsolete}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*yewg-}} From {{inh|en|enm|joinen}}, {{m|enm|joynen}}, {{m|enm|joignen}}, from {{der|en|fro|joindre}}, {{m|fro|juindre}}, {{m|fro|jungre}}, from {{der|en|la|iungō|t=join, yoke|pos=verb}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*yewg-|gloss=to join, unite}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|iucian}}, {{m|ang|iugian}}, {{m|ang|ġeocian}}, {{m|ang|ġyċċan|t=to join; yoke}}. More at {{m|en|yoke}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|join}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈd͡ʒɔɪn/}} * {{rhymes|en|ɔɪn|s=1}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-join.wav|a=GA}} * {{audio|en|en-us-join.ogg|a=US}} * {{hyphenation|en|join}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb|4=joined,joint}} # {{senseid|en|combine}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To [[connect]] or [[combine]] into one; to put together. #: {{ux|en|The plumber '''joined''' the two ends of the broken pipe.}} #: {{ux|en|We '''joined''' our efforts to get an even better result.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To come together; to meet. #: {{ux|en|Parallel lines never '''join'''.}} #: {{ux|en|These two rivers '''join''' in about 80 miles.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To enter into [[association]] or [[alliance]], to [[unite]] in a [[common]] [[purpose]]. #* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|part=1|scene=ii|page=26|passage=Forſake thy king and do but '''ioyne''' with me
And we will triumph ouer al the world.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare King John|act=3|scene=i|page=8|column=2|passage={{...}}Nature and Fortune '''ioyn’d''' to make thee great.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To start working on or participating in a project. #: {{ux|en|He '''joined''' season 2 of the television show.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To come into the [[company]] of. #: {{ux|en|I will '''join''' you in watching the football game as soon as I have finished my work.}} #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|IV|46|No matter how early I came down, I would find him on the veranda, smoking cigarettes, or otherwise his man would be there with a message to say that his master would shortly '''join''' me if I would kindly wait.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To become a [[member]] of. #: {{ux|en|Many children '''join''' a sports club.}} #: {{ux|en|Most politicians have '''joined''' a party.}} #* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=22|passage=In the autumn there was a row at some cement works about the unskilled labour men. A union had just been started for them and all but a few '''joined'''. One of these blacklegs was laid for by a picket and knocked out of time.}} # {{lb|en|computing|databases|transitive}} To produce an [[intersection]] of [[data]] in two or more [[database]] [[table]]s. #: {{ux|en|By '''joining''' the Customer table on the Product table, we can show each customer's name alongside the products they have ordered.}} # To unite in marriage. #* {{RQ:Book of Common Prayer|chapter=Of Matrimony|folio=xiii|passage=Into the whiche holy eſtate theſe two perſones pꝛeſent: come nowe to be '''ioyned'''.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare As You Like It|III|iii|198|2|{{...}}this fellow wil but '''ioyne''' you together, as they ioyne
Wainscot, then one of you wil proue a ſhrunke pannell{{...}}}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Matthew|19|6|page=1241|column=2|text=What therefore God hath '''ioyned''' together, let not man put aſunder.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|rare}} To [[enjoin]] upon; to [[command]]. #* {{RQ:Tyndale Obedience|chapter=Anoylynge|folio=Cxj|passage=And they '''ioyne''' them penaunce / as they call it / to faſt / to goo pylgremages ⁊ geve ſo moch to make ſatiſfaccion with all.}} # To accept, or engage in, as a contest. #: {{ux|en|to '''join''' encounter, battle, or issue}} #* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|part=1|scene=i|page=29|passage=Then when our powers in points of ſwords are '''ioin’d'''
And cloſde in compaſſe of the killing bullet, {{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=6|passage=On the rough edge of battel ere it '''joyn'd'''.|year=1873}} #* {{quote-book |en |year=1965 |author=w:Cho-yun Hsu |title=Ancient China in Transition: An Analysis of Social Mobility, 722–222 {{smallcaps|b.c.}} |url=https://archive.org/details/ancientchinaintr0000hsuc/ |publisher=w:Stanford University Press |LCCN=65-13110 |OCLC=460657230 |page=19 |pageurl=https://archive.org/details/ancientchinaintr0000hsuc/page/19/ |passage=Before '''joining''' battle, the officers and warriors gathered to make divinations "before the spirits of the former rulers," as at the battle of Yen-ling between Chin and Ch'u in 575 {{smallcaps|b.c.}}}} ====Conjugation==== {{en-conj|old=1}} ====Synonyms==== * {{sense|to combine more than one item into one}} {{l|en|bewed}}, {{l|en|connect}}, {{l|en|fay}}, {{l|en|unite}};
